safety_notes: Have spouse present during all standing exercises
Stop immediately if dizzy - sit and wait 5 min
Use wall or chair for support during balance work
Watch for overexertion signs due to blood thinner

exercises.name: Seated Marching
exercises.description: Gentle warm-up activating hip flexors and leg coordination with focus on left leg
steps: Sit tall, feet flat, hands on armrests
Lift RIGHT knee 2-3 inches, hold 2 sec, lower slowly
Lift LEFT knee (assist under thigh if needed), hold 2 sec, lower slowly
Alternate, spending extra focus on left leg
tips: Any left leg lift is progress
Focus mentally on left leg - brain connection is key
exercises.easier: Slide left foot forward/back instead of lifting
exercises.harder: Lift knee higher or try without assisting left leg

exercises.name: Seated Weight Shifts (Side to Side)
exercises.description: Improve weight distribution awareness to reduce fall risk
steps: Sit on front half of chair, feet flat, hands on thighs
Shift weight to RIGHT hip over 3 sec, hold 5 sec, return to center
Shift weight to LEFT hip over 3 sec, hold 7-10 sec
Return to center, repeat
tips: Slow controlled movement only
Spend extra time on left side
exercises.easier: Smaller shifts or keep hands on armrests
exercises.harder: Hold 10 sec each, or lift opposite foot 1 inch during hold
warnings: Don't shift far enough to feel unstable

exercises.name: Supported Standing Hold
exercises.description: Build standing balance confidence and leg strength
steps: Spouse beside you, chair in front
Lean forward, push through legs to stand using arms as needed
Hold lightly on chair back, stand tall, breathe normally
Hold 15 sec, then lower slowly back to seated
tips: Don't rush transitions - falls happen during sit-to-stand
Look straight ahead, not at feet
exercises.easier: Hold 5-10 sec, or keep more weight on arms
exercises.harder: Hold 20-30 sec, or use fingertips only

exercises.name: Seated Knee Extensions
exercises.description: Strengthen quads for standing, walking, and stair climbing
steps: Sit tall, hands on armrests
Straighten RIGHT knee, toes up, hold 3 sec, lower slowly
Repeat all right reps, then switch to LEFT leg
Assist left lift with hands under thigh if needed
tips: Any left lift counts
Control the lowering phase - it builds strength too
exercises.easier: Partial extension, or 6-8 reps per leg

exercises.name: Sit-to-Stand Practice (Partial)
exercises.description: Build strength for standing - one of the most functional movements for independence
steps: Sit at front edge, feet slightly behind knees
Lean forward - nose over toes, look ahead
Push through legs and arms to stand 60-70% of the way
Hold partial stand 2 sec, lower with control over 3 sec
tips: Nose over toes is key
Lowering slowly builds more strength than going up
exercises.easier: Rise only 30-40%, or use arms more
warnings: Stop if knees hurt or dizzy

exercises.name: Seated Hamstring & Hip Stretches
exercises.description: Cool-down for leg and hip flexibility
steps: Hamstring: extend leg, heel on floor, lean forward gently - 20 sec per leg
Hip flexor (figure-4): ankle on opposite knee, press knee down - 20 sec per side
Glute: hug knee to chest - 15 sec per side
5 deep breaths to finish
tips: Hip flexor stretch especially important for cane users
Left side less flexible - be patient
exercises.easier: 10-15 sec holds, skip figure-4 if too difficult
warnings: Care with hip flexor if you have hip replacement

exercises.name: Seated Torso Rotations
exercises.description: Warm up spine and core, improve rotational mobility for daily tasks
steps: Sit tall, arms crossed over chest
Rotate upper body to look over RIGHT shoulder, hold 2 sec
Return to center, rotate to LEFT, hold 2 sec
Keep hips square - only upper body rotates
tips: Breathe normally throughout
Reduce range if you feel back pinching
exercises.harder: 4-sec hold, or add side reach at end of rotation
warnings: Move slowly if history of vertigo

exercises.name: Seated Marching with Arm Swing
exercises.description: Coordination exercise combining opposite arm/leg movement - mimics walking pattern
steps: Lift RIGHT knee while swinging LEFT arm forward
Lower right knee while bringing left arm back
Lift LEFT knee while swinging RIGHT arm forward
Continue alternating smoothly - smaller left side movements are OK
tips: Opposite arm and leg is the natural walking pattern
Reset and continue if you mix up the pattern
exercises.easier: Legs only first, add arms when comfortable
exercises.harder: Increase speed or exaggerate arm swing

exercises.name: Standing Weight Shifts (Supported)
exercises.description: Progress to standing balance - shifting weight while holding support
steps: Stand facing counter, both hands lightly holding, spouse beside you
Shift weight onto RIGHT foot, hold 3 sec, return to center
Shift weight onto LEFT foot, hold 5 sec, return to center
Repeat
tips: Both feet stay on floor throughout
Keep hands light - building independent balance
warnings: Stop immediately if dizzy or unstable

exercises.name: Bilateral Shoulder Raises
exercises.description: Strengthen shoulders and practice bilateral arm lifting for dressing and reaching
equipment: Light resistance band or 1-2 lb weights (optional)
steps: Sit tall, arms at sides
Raise both arms forward to shoulder height, hold 2 sec, lower slowly
8 reps forward, then 8 reps lifting arms out to sides
Focus on left arm keeping pace with right
tips: Left arm won't go as high - expected
Use right arm as visual guide for left to follow
exercises.easier: Lift arms 45° only, or assist left arm with right hand
exercises.harder: Resistance band between hands, or 1-2 lb weights
warnings: Don't force left arm past comfortable range

exercises.name: Left Arm Assisted Reach & Grasp
exercises.description: Neuroplasticity work to rebuild left arm function for daily tasks
equipment: Small objects: water bottle, cup, ball
steps: Sit at table, objects 8-10 inches in front
Use right hand to position left hand on table
Slide left arm forward to reach object, assist grasp with right hand if needed
Try to contribute with left hand even if minimally - hold 3 sec, release and repeat
tips: Intense mental focus on left hand - brain is rewiring
Even 10% contribution from left hand is valuable
exercises.easier: Objects closer (4-6 inches), more right hand assistance
exercises.harder: Objects 12 inches away, right hand hovering only

exercises.name: Sit-to-Stand (Full Stand)
exercises.description: Progress to full standing from seated - building toward independence
steps: Sit at front edge, feet slightly behind knees, nose over toes
Push through legs and arms to fully stand
Stand tall 2 sec, lower slowly over 3-4 sec with control
Spouse nearby, letting you do the work
tips: Controlled lowering builds the most strength
Try to use legs more than arms
exercises.easier: Stand 80% of the way, or use arms more
exercises.harder: Hands hovering over armrests without gripping
warnings: Stop if knees hurt or dizzy

exercises.name: Seated Warm-up Circuit
exercises.description: Review of key movements from the week
steps: Ankle pumps x10
Seated marching x10 per leg
Knee extensions x8 per leg
Torso rotations x6 each side
Shoulder rolls x10
Move between exercises with minimal rest
tips: Notice what feels easier than Monday
Good standalone warm-up going forward
exercises.easier: Rest between each exercise, halve reps
warnings: Stop if any exercise causes pain

exercises.name: Standing Balance Holds (Progressed)
exercises.description: Progressed standing hold - finger-lifting to reduce arm dependence
steps: Stand at counter, spouse nearby, both hands lightly holding
Hold 20 sec (progressed from 15 sec)
If stable: lift one finger at a time, working toward 3-4 fingers only
Rest fully between sets
tips: Finger-lifting is optional but try it
Compare to Monday - this is your progress test
exercises.easier: All 10 fingers on counter, or 15-sec hold
warnings: Never zero hand support in week 1

exercises.name: Left Arm & Hand Dexterity Work
exercises.description: Dedicated left hand neuroplasticity practice for daily function
equipment: Objects: water bottle, ball, playing cards, therapy putty (if available)
steps: Large grasp: pick up and release larger objects x10
Fine motor: pick up playing cards one at a time (right hand assist OK)
Opposition: touch left thumb to each fingertip x5 (right hand assists positioning)
Functional grasp: hold fork, spoon, cup - daily items
tips: Mental focus on left hand is critical - brain rewiring in action
Celebrate any movement no matter how small
exercises.easier: Larger objects only, more right hand assistance
exercises.harder: Smaller objects, reduce right hand assistance
